{{short description|Norwegian experimental physicist and politician}}
'''Harald Trefall''' (10 November 1925 – 14 March 2008) was a [[Norway|Norwegian]] professor of [[experimental physics]] and [[far-right]] politician. He graduated from and worked at the [[University of Bergen]], where he focused his work on [[Cosmic ray|cosmic radiation]], and held a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Oslo]]. His political career started as a [[Bergen]] city councillor for the [[Progress Party (Norway)|Progress Party]] in 1983, until he left the party in 1986 and finished his term as an [[independent (politician)|independent]]. He worked within various anti-immigration organisations in the late 1980s, and founded the [[Fatherland Party (Norway)|Fatherland Party]] in 1990. He was a [[Hordaland County Municipality|Hordaland]] county councillor for this new party from 1991 to 1995.

==Professional career and life==
Trefall was born in [[Bergen]] on 10 November 1925.<ref name=aft1>{{cite news|url=http://onlinesos.aftenposten.no/tjenester/archive/show.htm?catalog=54452&page=10&query=%22harald+trefall%22&date=10.11.1975|work=[[Aftenposten]]|date=11 November 1975|title=Professor Harald Trefall fyller 50 år|accessdate=21 May 2011|language=Norwegian|page=10}}</ref> He graduated with a [[Academic degree|degree]] in mathematics and natural sciences at the University of Bergen in 1951, with an average of 1.21 or "exceptionally well".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://onlinesos.aftenposten.no/tjenester/archive/show.htm?catalog=15453&page=2&query=%22harald+trefall%22&date=20.6.1951|location=Bergen|work=[[Aftenposten]]|accessdate=21 May 2011|language=Norwegian|date=20 June 1951|title=Embetseksamen med innstilling Bergen|page=2}}</ref> He became [[amanuensis]] at the same university in 1955, [[docent]] of physics in 1957, and was appointed professor of experimental physics from 1 April 1964. He obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Oslo]] in 1961 for six [[Thesis|dissertations]] concerning topics within cosmic radiation. His initial academic area was cosmic radiation, but in 1962 he started researching [[X-ray]] phenomena brought forth by [[electron ionization|electron bombardment]] of the [[Atmosphere of Earth|upper atmosphere]] in the zone of the [[Aurora (astronomy)|polar aurora]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://onlinesos.aftenposten.no/tjenester/archive/show.htm?catalog=24194&page=12&query=%22harald+trefall%22&date=11.4.1964|page=12|title=Trefall professor i eksperimentell fysikk|work=[[Aftenposten]]|date=11 April 1964|accessdate=21 May 2011|language=Norwegian}}</ref> He became internationally known for his balloon experiments at the Physics Institute at the University of Bergen, and initiated a cooperation with the Max Planck Institute of [[West Germany]] in the early 1960s.<ref name=aft1/> He retired as professor in 1995.<ref name=aft3>{{cite news|url=http://onlinesos.aftenposten.no/tjenester/archive/show.htm?catalog=78658&page=11&query=%22harald+trefall%22&date=10.11.2000|page=11|title=75 år|work=[[Aftenposten]]|date=10 November 2000|accessdate=21 May 2011|language=Norwegian}}</ref> Trefall died 82 years old in March 2008.<ref>{{cite news|work=[[Bergens Tidende]]|title=Det er med sorg eg konstaterar|page=4|date=31 March 2008|first=Lars Bjarne|last=Marøy|language=Norwegian}}</ref><ref>Death announcement, ''Bergens Tidende'' 18 March 2008</ref>

==Political career==
Trefall started his political career in the [[1983 Norwegian local elections|1983 local elections]] when he was elected as a city councillor for the Progress Party in Bergen.<ref name=aft3/><ref>{{cite news|work=[[Bergens Tidende]]|title=Professor med meninger|date=10 November 1995|page=30|language=Norwegian}}</ref> He left the party in 1986<ref>{{cite news|work=[[Norwegian News Agency]]|title=Utmelding fra Bergen Fremskrittsparti|date=15 April 1986|language=Norwegian}}</ref> because he thought that it no longer followed its own political program, and claimed that he finished his term by only representing the party's program, rather than its party group. He believed that the party really wanted to open the borders, and that its policy thus was too liberal with regards to immigration.<ref name=aft2/> Trefall was one of the founders of ''[[Folkebevegelsen mot innvandring]]'' (FMI) in 1987.<ref>{{cite news|work=[[Norwegian News Agency]]|title=Folkeaksjonen mot innvandring er stiftet|date=4 October 1987|location=[[Haugesund]]|language=Norwegian}}</ref> For the [[1989 Norwegian parliamentary election|1989 parliamentary election]], he headed the list of the [[Stop Immigration]] party in [[Hordaland]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://onlinesos.aftenposten.no/tjenester/archive/show.htm?catalog=75221&page=8&query=%22harald+trefall%22&date=24.9.1988|work=[[Aftenposten]]|date=24 September 1988|accessdate=21 May 2011|language=Norwegian|title=Partiet Stopp Innvandringen vil inn på Stortinget: Kjentfolk stiller ved 89-valg|page=8|first=Kurt-Johnny|last=Olsen}}</ref> He founded the Fatherland Party in 1990, and was elected as a [[Hordaland County Municipality|Hordaland]] [[county council (Norway)|county councillor]] following the [[1991 Norwegian local elections|1991 local elections]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://onlinesos.aftenposten.no/tjenester/archive/show.htm?catalog=41133&page=49&query=%22harald+trefall%22&date=13.9.1991|work=[[Aftenposten]]|date=13 September 1991|accessdate=21 May 2011|language=Norwegian|title=Fedrelandspartiet på fylkestinget|page=49}}</ref> In 1993, he was part of a joint Scandinavian meeting of immigration opponents in [[Oslo]], where notably Denmark's [[Mogens Glistrup]] was egged and beaten up by youth from the [[Blitz (movement)|Blitz movement]] and [[SOS Rasisme]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://onlinesos.aftenposten.no/tjenester/archive/show.htm?catalog=71783&page=3&query=%22harald+trefall%22&date=25.10.1993|first=Arild S.|last=Johannessen|work=[[Aftenposten]]|date=25 October 1993|accessdate=21 May 2011|language=Norwegian|title=Innvandringsmotstandere jaget|page=3}}</ref>

==Political views==
Trefall's main political concern was the recent immigration to Norway. He considered the new ethnic groups to be a threat to Norwegian [[homogeneity]], and believed that it would be devastating for the country in the long run. His solution for helping those in need, was to support them in local [[refugee camp]]s, rather than letting them come to Norway.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://onlinesos.aftenposten.no/tjenester/archive/show.htm?catalog=74051&page=60&query=%22harald+trefall%22&date=9.11.1987|accessdate=21 May 2011|language=Norwegian|date=9 November 1987|title=Flyktningdebatt uten rabalder|first=Bjørn|last=Olsen|page=60|work=[[Aftenposten]]}}</ref> Although he stated that all humans were of equal worth, he voiced support for [[Nativism (politics)|nativism]], arguing that each country's native citizens should be given special preferential rights in relation to migrants and refugees.<ref name=aft2/>

He was also opposed to the [[European Economic Community]] (later the [[European Union]]), which he believed would eventually collapse like the [[Soviet Union]]. He thought that the principle of [[open borders]] would destroy the common fellowship and good camaraderie between countries.<ref name="aft2">{{cite news|last=Indrøy|first=Rune|date=9 November 1990|title=- Landenes borgere må gis særrettigheter|language=Norwegian|page=10|work=[[Aftenposten]]|url=http://onlinesos.aftenposten.no/tjenester/archive/show.htm?catalog=70279&page=10&query=%22harald+trefall%22&date=9.11.1990|url-access=subscription|accessdate=21 May 2011}}{{Dead link|date=July 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In 2001 he argued that the demand voiced by [[Lars Sponheim]] for increased work-based immigration to Norway was evocative of the "slave-owner ideology" of former colonial societies, such as the [[Slavery in the United States|slaveholding United States]]. In addition, he held that [[Thorbjørn Jagland]] expressed racist attitudes when he promoted immigration to Norway in order to make immigrants take the "dirty jobs" Norwegians would not accept. He maintained that the immigrants in turn would become just as selective as the Norwegians, which in turn would require a corresponding increase of immigration.<ref>{{cite news|last=Trefall|first=Harald|date=14 August 2001|title=Slaveholder-ideologi|language=Norwegian|work=[[Bergens Tidende]]|url=http://www.bt.no/meninger/Slaveholder-ideologi-2374308.html|url-status=dead|accessdate=21 May 2011|archive-date=18 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120918025608/http://www.bt.no/meninger/Slaveholder-ideologi-2374308.html}}</ref>
